sources.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories

articles.author: Chandelis Duster
articles.description: Congress recently gave the Department of Transportation $12.5 billion to upgrade the aging air traffic control system. President Trump wants more.
articles.title: Flight disruptions expected to last into Monday

articles.author: Ava Pukatch
articles.description: NASA's Voyager 1, which is the furthest man-made object from Earth, is set to reach a new milestone this week. On Wednesday, the probe will be roughly 16 billion miles from Earth.
articles.title: Far from home. Voyager 1 is now farther than anything man has sent into space

articles.author: Diaa Hadid
articles.description: Sydney Sweeney has great jeans, American Eagle Outfitters tells us. But who made them? And what are working conditions like in the garment factories of Pakistan and Bangladesh?
articles.title: Who makes Sydney Sweeney's American Eagle jeans — and under what conditions?

articles.author: Ava Pukatch
articles.description: Officials are seeking at least $1 million in damages from the owners of the tanker that hit a cruise ship last week. The incident was dubbed "the miracle on the Mississippi" after no one was killed.
articles.title: New Orleans port sues owners of tanker involved in Mississippi crash

articles.author: Saige Miller
articles.description: In several states, Democrats took control of legislatures that had been divided and they weakened GOP dominance in others. Issues on the agenda: More access to health care, new limits on school vouchers.
articles.title: Midterm voters ended the long-running GOP dominance in state legislatures

articles.author: Julie Depenbrock
articles.description: A year ago in November, New Mexico became the first state to offer free childcare to every eligible family, regardless of income.
articles.title: New Mexico wanted free childcare for all. This is what's worked — and what hasn't

articles.author: Jonaki Mehta
articles.description: The film Being Heumann tells the lesser-known story of the mother of the disability rights movement. A new generation of activists share how they "carry the torch" today.
articles.title: A new generation of disability rights activists carry on Judy Heumann's legacy

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: A federal judge on Saturday ordered a two-week delay to any work at a historic Washington public golf course not far from the White House.
articles.title: Trump blasts judge for halting his Washington golf project and says he will appeal

articles.author: Chandelis Duster
articles.description: Some college football games were delayed a few hours on Saturday or postponed to Sunday. And in Oklahoma at least, there will be perks for fans to make up for the inconvenience, including cheap beers.
articles.title: FAA ground stop disrupts college football

articles.author: Marissa J. Lang
articles.description: A new Florida law that prohibits taxpayer dollars from going toward diversity initiatives has prompted Delray Beach to cancel its St. Patrick's Day parade after a nearly 60-year run.
articles.title: Florida city cancels St. Patrick's Day parade, citing new anti-DEI law

articles.author: Krishani Dhanji
articles.description:
Independent MP says she is ‘overwhelmed’ by thousands of warm wishes and thanks Australians for charity donations

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The independent Australian MP Helen Haines has been discharged from hospital, four weeks after she was allegedly attacked by a man outside her electorate office in Victoria resulting in the double amputation of her legs.
In a statement, Haines said she had moved to the rehabilitation stage of her recovery, which would continue in Melbourne.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: MP Helen Haines’s first words since leaving hospital after alleged attack led to double amputation

articles.author: Denis Campbell and Hanad Ahmed
articles.description:
NHS chiefs said last year that 43% of maternity and neonatal units in England do not meet safety standards
Ministers have been accused of “gambling with the safety of mothers and babies” after admitting they do not know how much repairing decrepit maternity units would cost.
NHS chiefs said last year that shoddy infrastructure meant 43% of maternity and neonatal units in England did not meet basic safety standards. Infrastructure problems hampered the delivery of clinical care thousands of times every year, NHS England said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ministers accused of ‘gambling with safety’ for not knowing cost of NHS maternity unit repairs

articles.author: Sam Jones in Madrid
articles.description:
Country’s sixth general election in 11 years could lead to far-right role in government for first time since Franco’s death
Spaniards head to the polls on 29 November to vote in the country’s sixth general election in 11 years. The snap election could end eight years of socialist-led rule and bring a far-right party into government for the first time since Spain’s return to democracy after the death of Gen Franco.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Will Spain’s snap election in November bring a far-right party into government?

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Ahead of Apec summit, PM says ‘Canada is going to move forward either way’ when asked if Chinese investment was leverage in US negotiations
The prime minister of Canada, Mark Carney, said the country could turn to Chinese automakers if trade negotiations with the US president, Donald Trump, failed to preserve an integrated North American auto industry.
Carney’s comments in Cambodia on Monday came ahead of a planned meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping this week in Shenzhen, China, where auto manufacturing is expected to be discussed. The two leaders reached an agreement in January allowing tens of thousands of Chinese electric vehicles into Canada at reduced tariffs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canada could work with Chinese automakers if US trade talks fail, says Carney

articles.author: Australian Associated Press
articles.description:
Supermarket giant says no customer, team or supplier data compromised but recommends updating passwords as a precaution

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s second-largest retailer has been targeted in a cyber-attack, though it is still too early to tell whether any of its data has been stolen or compromised.
Coles revealed the threat on Monday morning, saying it was investigating with support from the Australian Cyber Security Centre and global security experts.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Coles investigates cyber-attack and apologises to customers

articles.author: Nick Visser
articles.description:
Students left in limbo after digital platform fails during exams, with university saying ‘third-party technical partners’ likely to blame for issue

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Hundreds of students at the University of Melbourne were forced to abandon their final exams on Monday morning after many were unable to access the digital platform needed to begin them.
Jol Scobie, a first-year student at the university, was set to take his Australian politics exam on Monday after preparing for weeks. He had initially been told earlier in the year it was going to be a hand-written essay before instructors changed the test to a digital platform.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tech failure forces hundreds of University of Melbourne students to abandon final exams mid-test

articles.author: Andrew Messenger
articles.description:
New National Health and Medical Research Council guidelines at odds with public hospital bans in Queensland and NT

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The federal health minister, Mark Butler, says he’s confident Queensland and Northern Territory will consider the advice of Australia’s “pre-eminent authority” over their bans on puberty blockers for transgender children.
The federal government last year commissioned the commonwealth-funded National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC) to develop the advice in response to bans in public hospitals imposed by the two governments.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia’s national medical research body advises conditional use of puberty blockers for transgender children

articles.author: Nino Bucci Justice and courts reporter
articles.description:
Victoria police allege man, suspected of being a chapter president of the gang, sent ‘threats and harassing text messages’ to Nine journalist

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A senior Hells Angel has been charged with threatening to kill Nine’s investigative reporter Nick McKenzie, the Victorian police taskforce investigating corruption in the building sector has confirmed.
Police said detectives from the taskforce had charged a man on Monday, after he “sent a number of allegedly threatening, offensive and abusive text messages” to the Age journalist on Friday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Senior Hells Angels bikie charged with threatening to kill investigative reporter Nick McKenzie

articles.author: Luca Ittimani and Associated Press
articles.description:
Company insists Alice Huang, who is accused of being a Chinese spy, left business in late 2025

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Megaspeed International, the company linked to the downfall of the Nvidia chief, Jensen Huang, says it is a “legitimate and lawful business” and has announced that its director, who allegedly had an affair with Jensen Huang, left the business in late 2025.
The Singapore-based cloud computing company on the weekend said it was “aware of recent media reports containing assertions about our business, supply chain and global operations that are not supported by verifiable evidence”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Megaspeed, the company linked to the downfall of Nvidia boss, says it’s a ‘legitimate and lawful business’

articles.author: Dan Collyns and Associated Press
articles.description:
Pontiff delivers forceful speech on final day in Peru as he travels from high in the Andes into the Amazon
Pope Leo XIV has demanded justice for environmental defenders killed for protecting the Amazon and backed efforts by Indigenous peoples to stop their lands from being ravaged by logging and illegal mining.
On the penultimate day of his South American tour, Leo on Sunday travelled into the Peruvian Amazon and channelled one of Pope Francis’s core teachings that links care for the most vulnerable with care for God’s creation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘The blood of these brothers cries out’: Pope Leo demands justice for people killed protecting the Amazon

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Silicon Valley figures back CEO ousted after revelations of affair with suspected Chinese spy, as US treasury secretary urges Nvidia to carry out ‘dramatic shake-up’
Elon Musk and a host of other tech executives are among more than 165,000 signatories of an open letter calling for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia chief, days after he resigned from the multi-trillion dollar chip company.
The letter demands that the company’s board members “bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Elon Musk joins 165,000 others calling for Nvidia to bring back Jensen Huang in open letter

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Large waves up to 50ft flooded southern California streets and prompted evacuation warning near coastal city
The California coast was pummeled again on Sunday by huge waves that inundated beaches, flooded local streets and forced the closure of popular piers.
The National Weather Service office for the San Francisco Bay Area warned that surf up to 35ft (11 meters) was possible, along with dangerous rip currents and sneaker waves.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Huge waves pummel California coast, forcing closure of popular piers

articles.author: Hannah Al-Othman
articles.description:
Survey respondents describe current or former partners controlling bank accounts and taking out credit online without full consent
Almost one in five young women and girls in the UK have experienced digital financial products being used as a tool of abuse by a current or former partner, a report has found.
Abusers are exploiting banking apps, online payments and digital credit to control young women, causing financial harm and preventing them from leaving relationships, according to research from the charity Surviving Economic Abuse.
In the UK, call the national domestic abuse helpline on 0808 2000 247, or visit Women’s Aid. In the US, the domestic violence hotline is 1-800-799-SAFE (7233). In Australia, the national family violence counselling service is on 1800 737 732. Other international helplines may be found via www.befrienders.org
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Digital finance products used to abuse almost 20% of young women and girls, UK report finds

articles.author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
articles.description:
Prime minister promises ‘root-and-branch rethink’ of support for young people as Milburn report advises sweeping changes to some benefits 

Andy Burnham: The crisis facing Britain’s young people is politicians’ fault. To fix it, we need a generational response

Andy Burnham has pledged to intervene as early as childhood to tackle youth unemployment before a watershed review, promising “a root-and-branch rethink of how we support childhood in the modern world”.
Burnham said the government would intervene at all the stages of life in which young people fell behind, and “long before they find themselves out of work and reliant on the state”, including providing more opportunities for vocational training in schools.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham pledges early intervention and ‘benefits backstop’ to tackle youth jobs crisis

articles.author: Lyndsey Winship
articles.description:
Exclusive: Trailer released for Rambert’s version of Russell T Davies’s show about friendship amid the 80s Aids crisis and the ‘extraordinary freedom’ of clubbing
Russell T Davies’s award-winning series It’s a Sin, about young gay friends living through the Aids crisis in 1980s London, is getting a new life as a dance piece, with a trailer released on Monday ahead of an opening at Aviva Studios in Manchester in February.
“We had a few approaches, but a lot of people wanted to make it a musical, which made my heart sink slightly,” said Davies. “I always imagined an aria between those two women on the seafront at the end and I thought: ‘Oh, that could be so terrible!’” Dance was different, he said. “It felt so original and so pure. The story distils down to these emotional moments that are going to be done so beautifully on stage.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Loaded with potential’: stage version of TV smash It’s a Sin has the dancefloor at its heart

articles.author: Coral Murphy Marcos
articles.description:
Tank vessel suffered sudden steering failure two minutes before slamming into docked riverboat near New Orleans
Federal safety investigators with the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) recovered audio and released a preliminary timeline on Sunday of a collision between a cruise ship and a tanker vessel in the Mississippi River on Friday.
The data was retrieved after more than 30 people were injured when a tanker collided with a docked cruise ship – American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage riverboat – near the port of New Orleans on Friday at about 12.30pm. All passengers aboard the cruise ship have been accounted for, officials said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US officials recover audio from ‘Mississippi miracle’ cruise ship and tanker crash

articles.author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
articles.description:
Professor urges ministers to use awareness triggered by Russell Brand conviction to examine use of rape myths in trials
The debate triggered by high-profile cases must “pull back the curtain” on the treatment of people making allegations of sexual offences in the criminal justice system in England and Wales, the government’s independent adviser on rape has told the Guardian.
Prof Katrin Hohl, who has advised the government in an overhaul of how rape is treated by police forces and the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), said the government should use the public awareness triggered by Russell Brand’s conviction for rape to examine the use of rape myths and jury direction in trials.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Pull back the curtain’ on treatment of sexual assault victims in court, says UK government adviser

articles.author: Jakub Krupa
articles.description:
Authorities say Russian intelligence service ordered attack which Estonian PM links to Tallinn’s support for Ukraine 
Estonia will close all its border crossings with Russia from 1 December after a suspected sabotage attack on a drone maker in the Baltic state over the weekend, which authorities said was ordered by Russia’s GRU military intelligence service.
On Saturday morning, eight people were detained during an attempted attack on Threod Systems, a defence company that manufactures long-range attack and reconnaissance drones. No injuries or damage were reported after the company’s security team responded to the incident.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Estonia to close all border crossings with Russia after attack on drone maker

articles.author: Harry Taylor
articles.description:
Duke of Sussex meets wounded veterans in city and says country could one day host Invictus Games
Prince Harry has told Ukrainian soldiers they are going to win the war with Russia, during a surprise visit to the country.
The Duke of Sussex met wounded veterans and medics in the city of Lviv, in the west of Ukraine, as he addressed a conference on treating those injured in war. He said he had taken a risk in travelling to the country, but that he had felt “warmth” when arriving on Saturday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Prince Harry tells Ukrainians they are ‘going to win war’ on surprise trip to Lviv

articles.author: Michael Sainato
articles.description:
Mohamed Yusuf is fighting for his life after alleged attack by passenger who said he did not like driver’s first name
A Somali-American Uber driver was allegedly brutally assaulted by a passenger in Hopkins, Minnesota, on Saturday, in what his family says “appears to be a hate crime”.
The driver, Mohamed Yusuf, is currently hospitalized and fighting for his life, his family told the Somali Brief, a digital news site run by two Somali American journalists. The driver’s cousin, Abdinasir Ali told the outlet that the alleged attack took place early Saturday after a passenger in Hopkins, a suburban city south-west of Minneapolis, asked Yusuf’s name and then said he did not like the name Mohamed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Somali-American Uber driver brutally assaulted in alleged hate crime in Minnesota

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Guard allegedly tried to flee traffic stop in Baton Rouge

Tigers say they are aware of situation involving player

LSU guard MiLaysia Fulwiley, one of the ninth-ranked Tigers’ leading scorers, was arrested after allegedly striking a police officer while attempting to flee from a traffic stop.
LSU’s athletic department, in a written statement provided to The Associated Press, said university officials “are aware of the situation and have no further comment at this time as it’s an ongoing legal matter.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: LSU star MiLaysia Fulwiley arrested after allegedly striking police officer with car

articles.author: Rory Carroll
articles.description:
Estimated 350,000 people rally against plan to scrap licence fees and fund broadcasters from state budget
Hundreds of thousands of Czechs have rallied in Prague to protest against a perceived government attempt to stifle media freedom.
The gathering on Sunday to save the mandatory licence fees that fund Czechia’s public broadcasters drew more than 350,000 people, making it one of the biggest in the country’s history, organisers said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs protest in Prague over media freedom

articles.author: Rory Carroll and agencies
articles.description:
Strikes cast further doubt on peace talks between Tehran and Washington with increasing risk of escalation 
Iran has launched drone attacks against a US military base in Bahrain, casting further doubt on peace talks between Tehran and Washington and raising the spectre of escalation.
Blasts sounded over the Gulf nation on Sunday in the second Iranian drone attack in three days in retaliation for US strikes in Iran.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Iran launches drone attacks against US military base in Bahrain

articles.author: Frances Mao
articles.description:
Iran has targeted airbase in Bahrain in latest resumption of strikes since september
The state-run Bahrain news agency is also carrying the statements of each country in the region responding to Iran’s actions targeting their Gulf neighbour this morning.
Jordan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar have all strongly condemned the attack and expressed solidarity with Bahrain.
The Kingdom affirms that the Iranian attacks constitute a violation of international law and the principles of good neighborliness. The Kingdom stresses the importance of an immediate halt to the blatant Iranian attacks on the countries of the region, and of taking serious steps towards achieving security and stability for the countries of the region and their peoples.
The continuation of these attacks represents a dangerous escalation that will complicate efforts to contain the tension and undermine political and diplomatic endeavors aimed at achieving security and stability in the region.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed the Kingdom of Bahrain’s strongest condemnation of the continued Iranian aggression against its territory, including the attack launched today, Sunday, November 15, 2026, by drones that were intercepted and destroyed by air defense systems in the Kingdom’s airspace.
This comes two days after a similar attack at dawn on Friday, November 13, 2026, by two drones that were also intercepted. The Iranian Revolutionary Guard explicitly claimed responsibility for these attacks. The Ministry praised the efficiency, vigilance, and capability of the Bahrain Defense Force in confronting today’s attack and its complete readiness to deter any aggression.
 

 The Ministry considered these attacks a resumption of Iran’s heinous aggression against the Kingdom and countries in the region, disregarding the provisions of international law and the principles of the UN Charter.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, Egypt condemn Iranian attack on Bahrain - as it happened

articles.author: Agencies
articles.description:
Fears for national college entrance exam next week as test taker admits sending photos of questions to AI tool
The marks attained by the top scorer ⁠on South Korea’s national exam for aspiring tax accountants this year seemed too good to be true. On Sunday, sceptics were ⁠proven right when he ⁠confessed to ​using generative AI to cheat.
The scandal has followed months of speculation after he scored near-perfect marks on hundreds of questions over two exams ⁠taken in April and July. It has also raised the stakes for organisers of South Korea’s annual college entrance exam this Thursday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: 160 questions, only one wrong: top scorer in South Korea tax exam admits AI cheating

articles.author: Oliver Holmes and Kaamil Ahmed
articles.description:
International court of justice has never before found a state guilty of genocide, and ruling will have implications for case against Israel
The world’s top court will deliver a judgment this week on whether Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, in a landmark case that will set a critical 21st-century benchmark for the gravest of all international crimes.
The closely watched judgment could become one of the most significant moments in international law since the end of the second world war.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: World’s top court to rule if Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya

articles.author: Oliver Holmes and Rebecca Bailey
articles.description:
Tussle for influence as trade, tech and regional security to take centre stage in China, Philippines and Cambodia meetings
World leaders will fly in to Asia for back-to-back high-level summits this week against the backdrop of the tussle for influence between the superpowers China and the US.
Beijing will have the home advantage when it welcomes Donald Trump to its southern technology hub of Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) leaders’ meeting. It starts two weeks after the US leader lost midterm elections.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: World leaders head to Asia for back-to-back diplomatic summits

articles.author: Raphael Rashid
articles.description:
Filipino entry, pop and rap song Sobra-Sobra, takes 19-year-old to victory at grand final in Bangkok
Carmelle Collado has won the first Eurovision song contest Asia, taking the Philippines’ entry, Sobra-Sobra, to victory in Bangkok on Saturday night, at the first regional edition of the contest to be staged outside Europe.
Eleven countries competed at the One Bangkok Forum in central Bangkok, and the show ran for two and a half hours including advertising.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Philippines’ Carmelle wins first Eurovision contest in Asia

articles.author: Timothy Pratt
articles.description:
James ‘Fergie’ Chambers, a Cox Enterprises heir, faced a two-hour hearing about alleged support for Hamas
A two-hour hearing in Spain’s high court Friday on the US extradition request of wealthy leftwing activist and philanthropist James “Fergie” Chambers turned out to be a study in contrasts.
Chambers’s defense took most of the session to query the US citizen and detail irregularities in the Trump administration’s extradition request – several of which the Guardian has reported on – as well as the figures of Spanish law that would lead the three-judge panel to deny the request; while the prosecutor sped through his case, head down, asking Chambers no questions at all.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How a US extradition bid over Hamas allegations put a wealthy activist before a Spanish court

articles.author: Jonathan Watts; graphics by Sara Fiorillo
articles.description:
People around the world have contended with unprecedented weather events and their fatal effects caused by the climate catastrophe
After the world’s hottest summer since records began in 1850, the death toll from extreme weather in 2026 is already in the high tens of thousands. That is a conservative estimate and is certain to rise much higher.
As Cop31 continues and scientists warn that climate breakdown may be accelerating, the Guardian looks back at a year of droughts, fires and floods as a reminder that, unless the world takes urgent action to cut emissions, this disastrous year will be one of the best of the rest of our lives.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Choking fires, deadly heat and devastating floods: 2026 in extreme weather

articles.author: William Christou
articles.description:
Prime ministerial hopeful calls Arab minority ‘an integral part of the Israeli story’ as he seeks to form government
Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot condemned a “racist and aggressive campaign of delegitimisation” against the country’s Arab citizens, after the caretaker prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, accused Arab parties of electoral fraud without evidence.
Netanyahu has repeatedly targeted Arab parties and Palestinian citizens of Israel after his party received a disappointing electoral showing, accusing them of manipulating the election and being linked to Hamas. Israeli electoral authorities have rejected these claims as not being backed by evidence.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Eisenkot condemns Netanyahu’s ‘racist’ campaign against Israel’s Arab citizens

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
First direct attack on US military installations for months was in response to US airstrike on communications tower
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it has targeted and destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in response to a US airstrike on a communications tower in Sirik overlooking the strait of Hormuz. It is Iran’s first direct attack on US military installations for months.
“This is a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to end its aerial mischief and oil smuggling in the strait of Hormuz,” the IRGC said. “In the event of repeated violations and aggression, the IRGC aerospace force is on full alert to confront the enemy without constraint.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Iran says it targeted US military radar in Bahrain in retaliatory strike

articles.author: Ed Walton and Alice Nightingale-Smith for MetDesk
articles.description:
Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week 
Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations.
After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy. This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera. The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia. Further heavy rain is expected to fall in Italy and the Balkans over the next few days, with the latest forecast models indicating an additional 100mm could accumulate widely, while totals close to 200mm are likely in more mountainous areas.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe

articles.author: Sarah Johnson
articles.description:
Political prisoner Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, one of seven athletes at risk of execution in Iran, given prestigious Magnitsky humanitarian award 
A boxer and political prisoner on death row in Iran said he will “never surrender” as he accepted a prestigious human rights prize on behalf of “the generation that is paying the price of freedom with their lives”.
Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, an Iranian boxing champion, coach and political prisoner, has been sentenced to death three times and is one of seven athletes at risk of execution in Iran. He was given the Magnitsky award for outstanding human rights activist at a ceremony in London on Thursday night.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Boxer on death row in Iran vows ‘not to bow before oppression’ after winning rights prize

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg and agencies
articles.description:
After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’
The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation.
Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza cleared of using AI to write prize-winning story

articles.author: Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
Remains believed to have belonged to Africans or Afro-Brazilians repatriated after being flown back by diplomats 
Two skulls, including that of a man believed to have taken part in Brazil’s greatest slave revolt but whose remains were taken to the United States and used in racist eugenics studies at Harvard University, were repatriated on Wednesday.
The remains had been outside Brazil since the 19th century. One was taken about 190 years ago from Salvador, the capital of the state of Bahia; the other, about 160 years ago, from Rio de Janeiro – and were welcomed back in moving, subdued ceremonies in both cities.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two skulls likely belonging to enslaved people returned to Brazil after Harvard used them in eugenics studies

articles.author: Facundo Iglesia in Buenos Aires and agencies
articles.description:
Leonardo Bertulazzi, 74, awaiting extradition to Italy, reportedly used harness to flee custody
A 74-year-old former member of Italy’s radical Marxist group the Red Brigades has escaped from house arrest in Argentina, the country’s security ministry confirmed on Wednesday, after he reportedly hid his ankle monitor inside a tube of pork and lowered himself from a fifth-floor balcony.
Authorities placed Leonardo Bertulazzi under house arrest in Buenos Aires in 2024, prior to his extradition to Italy to serve a 27-year prison sentence. He had received the sentence in 1987 for joining a subversive association and belonging to an armed group.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ex-member of radical Marxist group scales balcony, escapes house arrest in Argentina

articles.author: Associated Press at the Rafah crossing
articles.description:
Seven-time F1 world champion tours border area and logistics warehouses operated by Egyptian Red Crescent
Lewis Hamilton has visited Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with the Gaza Strip to meet organisations sending humanitarian aid to the territory.
The seven-time Formula One world champion has spoken out about conflict and humanitarian crises in the region, and has called for peace. He has frequently posted on social media about children killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza and called for a ceasefire.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lewis Hamilton visits Egypt’s Rafah crossing and Gaza aid facilities

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Aakash Hassan in Delhi
articles.description:
Former prime minister faces death penalty upon return after being sentenced in absentia over deaths in 2024 uprising
Sheikh Hasina is “confident” she will return to Bangladesh in December, according to exiled members of her party, after the disgraced former prime minister applied for a new passport this week.
Hasina has been living in self-imposed exile since August 2024 when she was toppled from power by a mass uprising against her authoritarian rule. She crossed the border to India, where she has since been allowed to live freely in Delhi.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Disgraced former leader Sheikh Hasina plans return to Bangladesh from exile

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
From the assassinations of her husband and mother-in-law to press stonewalling under Modi, Belonging offers an insider’s account of India’s political evolution
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
Few love stories have been as closely entwined with a nation’s history as that of Sonia and Rajiv Gandhi. The former’s much-awaited political memoir, Belonging, offers a strikingly candid account of her journey from a small town in Italy to the highest echelons of power in India – all for love, she says.
The veteran Congress party leader has been fiercely protective of her personal world. In Belonging, she opens up for the first time about the extraordinary twists and turns of a life that has largely unfolded in full public view. (The Guardian’s Hannah Ellis-Petersen has a rare in-person interview with Gandhi, and you can read an excerpt from the book here.)
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Grenades, grief and a deepening political divide: five takeaways from Sonia Gandhi’s new memoir

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo
Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.
The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven

articles.author: Chris Osuh Community affairs correspondent
articles.description:
See My World, an event highlighting the pan-African thought via film, poetry and dance, builds on momentum sparked by local activists and creatives
African philosophies including exploring how lessons from the past can shape the present and near future have inspired a film festival coming to Manchester.
See My World, a day dedicated to independent creators from across the African diaspora in the north of England, will take place at the Contact theatre on 21 November.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How African philosophies inspired a new approach to staging film festivals in Manchester

articles.author: Rebecca Ratcliffe, Gloria Dickie and Elisângela Mendonça
articles.description:
Mumbai facility is part of Reliance Industries, owner of world’s biggest oil refinery and funder of controversial mega-zoo
The Prince of Wales’s Earthshot prize will host its forthcoming annual awards ceremony at a venue owned by the billionaire Ambani family conglomerate, drawing criticism from conservationists over their fossil fuel businesses and their foundation’s controversial mega-zoo.
A spokesperson for the Earthshot prize, which awards £1m to five winners every year to invest in conservation work, confirmed to the Guardian and the news outlet Mongabay that this year’s ceremony will be held at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai on 17 November.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Environmentalists criticise choice of Earthshot prize venue owned by fossil fuel firm

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
articles.description:
Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families
The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.
The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa found the cult leader guilty of the crimes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
A previously unseen family archive offers a glimpse into the Indian Nobel prize winner’s artistic process and personal relationships in his final years
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
It’s easy to run out of words to describe Rabindranath Tagore. The first non-European to win the Nobel prize in literature, Tagore was a Bengali poet, musician, novelist, philosopher, songwriter, painter, humanist and educator.
Born in 1861, Tagore left an indelible mark on the subcontinent’s literature, music, education and art. Among his enduring legacies are the national anthems of India and Bangladesh.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The private creative world of Rabindranath Tagore, the man Yeats called ‘greater than any of us’

articles.author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
articles.description:
Mississippi Democrat points to commitments Trump made: lower prices, halt endless wars and release Epstein files
After recently becoming the first Mississippi Democrat elected to the US Senate in more than four decades, Scott Colom pledged to try to ensure Donald Trump “follows through on the commitments” he made while successfully running for a second presidency in 2024.
Colom, while being interviewed by CNN host Dana Bash on Sunday, alluded to various campaign promises made by Trump – including lowering consumer prices, halting the seemingly endless wars waged under other presidential administrations, and fully releasing files related to the prosecution of Jeffrey Epstein, the late accused sex trafficker whose social circle encompassed the US and global elite.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Senator-elect Scott Colom vows to ensure Trump follows through on his promises

articles.author: Marina Dunbar
articles.description:
Progressive US senator calling for more inclusion within Democratic caucus cites openness to change among peers
Democratic US senator Chris Van Hollen on Sunday escalated his bid to lead his party’s incoming Senate majority rather than Chuck Schumer, asserting that he has a path to victory amid a dedicated campaign that includes a series of television appearances.
Van Hollen, a Maryland progressive, appeared on Sunday on CNN, ABC and Fox News as he continues to make his case for why his peers in the Senate should reject Schumer, who has led the Democratic caucus for nearly a decade.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Chris Van Hollen says he has path to win Senate leader over Chuck Schumer

articles.author: Michael Sainato
articles.description:
Democratic senator Chris Van Hollen says Trump administration has not properly invested existing funds
Donald Trump’s administration on Sunday blamed the travel chaos stemming from Friday’s four-hour nationwide flight stoppage on prior presidents as well as a lack of congressional funding – though a Democratic senator argued that the Trump administration hasn’t properly invested all of the funds it has already been given to implement needed air travel infrastructure upgrades.
“I take responsibility for what was given to me by prior administrations,” the US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, told CNN’s Dana Bash, a day after he said routine but necessary maintenance botched by a contractor had caused Friday’s Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop, leading to the delay or cancellation of thousands of flights throughout the weekend.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Transportation secretary Sean Duffy blames prior presidents and Congress for flight stoppage

articles.author: Michael Sainato
articles.description:
Two people injured after wingtip of Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck nose of United Parcel Service Boeing 767
Two planes collided with one another on a taxiway at Miami’s international airport on Saturday night – a day after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued an hours-long nationwide ground stop due to communication issues affecting multiple air traffic control centers.
In a statement, the Trump administration-led FAA said the wingtip of a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck the nose of a United Parcel Service Boeing 767 “while the airplanes were taxiing at Miami International Airport”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two planes collide on taxiway at Miami airport one day after national grounding

articles.author: Adria R Walker
articles.description:
Behind the Mississippi senator-elect’s victory is a coalition of groups that didn’t have a lot of money, but had collective power and post-Callais anger
Long before national political leaders and media were paying any attention, long before the Louisiana v Callais supreme court decision gutted the Voting Rights Act, Mississippi organizers were working to grow political participation and improve quality of life in a state that often ranks low on its residents’ health and wellbeing.
Activists’ momentum contributed to Democrat Scott Colom’s historic upset in the midterm elections. A loose coalition of about a dozen, mostly Black-led nonprofits or initiatives rallied residents after Callais, the April decision that set off a flurry of redistricting efforts across southern states. That case was not the sole impetus for organizing efforts across Mississippi, but it turned out thousands in the 20 May “Mississippi Fights Back” rally. Callais became the most recent opportunity to channel people’s frustrations and hopes into action – and to harness previous campaigns that go back years and even decades.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We gotta do something’: the coalition that helped elect Scott Colom to Senate

articles.author: Rachel Leingang
articles.description:
Incoming lawmakers have more in common with each other than they have divisions, even across ideological factions
Democrats who won in the midterms, including those in places previously considered off the blue map and those in Democratic strongholds, crafted their campaigns around economic populism and accountability.
Lawmakers in the anti-establishment incoming congressional class have more in common with each other than divisions, even across ideological factions. Voters sent a resounding message to work on affordability and rein in the Trump administration, and Democrats across the party have many more shared goals than Republicans, who face a more existential level of discord.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Progressive versus moderate? Democrats deny party rift as they head into new Congress

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
House members have responded to legitimate criticism with cynicism. Let’s not have another ‘Bernie bros’ moment
Before we get started, some ground rules. You are, of course, completely free to disagree with everything I have to say here. However, doing so might mean that you’re racist, homophobic and/or sexist. (Not to boast, but I have a lot of oppression cards to play.) So, you might want to tread carefully, OK?
That might sound ridiculous, but I don’t make the rules: I’m just taking a page from the corporate Democrat playbook. From Haley Stevens to Hakeem Jeffries, cynically weaponizing identity politics to ward off reasonable criticism seems to be all the rage.
Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Corporate Democrats are weaponizing identity politics to smear progressives | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Eric Berger
articles.description:
City has failed to build infrastructure that could reduce threat, and saw 400 fires, 83 injuries and 12 deaths this year
Fires from lithium-ion batteries, which power ebikes and scooters, have become regular occurrences in New York, causing deaths and fear among residents, but the city has failed to build infrastructure that could reduce the threat.
New York has seen a dramatic uptick this year in fires from the batteries. In 2025, there were 292 fires, 51 injuries and one death, according to the New York fire department (FDNY). This year, there have already been more than 400 fires, 83 injuries and 12 deaths.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Enough is enough’: rising number of deadly ebike battery fires spark fear in New York City

articles.author: Ariana Baio in Denver
articles.description:
At party’s ‘What’s Next’ conference, consensus is they need to act quickly, but over affordability or accountability is the question
What’s next for Democrats?
It’s the question thousands of Democrats, including lawmakers, strategists, pollsters, creators, organizers, staffers and 2028 presidential hopefuls are trying to answer at a three-day gathering in Denver, after a sweeping victory in the 2026 midterm elections.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We must deliver’: jubilant Democrats gather in Denver to chart way forward

articles.author: David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
Midterm elections have defanged the US president – leaving critics to worry about his next move in his ‘fat Elvis’ stage
It was just before 3am when Donald Trump entered a crowded Manhattan ballroom, greeted by chants of “USA! USA” and theme music from the Hollywood film Air Force One. On stage, two red “Make America great again” (Maga) caps were mounted in glass cases like holy relics.
That was the scene 10 years ago this week when Trump, a businessman and reality TV star, stunned the world by beating Hillary Clinton to the White House. A decade later an unlikely president is serving an unlikely second term. But in the wake of a humiliating vote of no confidence in last week’s midterm elections, he now enters an endgame wracked with uncertainty.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Will Trump’s lame duck presidency push him further beyond constraints of the law?

articles.author: Bernie Sanders
articles.description:
This is not a personality contest. This is a debate about the future of the Democratic party
The election for Democratic Senate leader between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen must be understood for what it is.
This is not a personality contest. This is a debate about the future of the Democratic party. It is a debate about whether the Democratic party remains a top-down party dominated by billionaire campaign contributors, inside-the-beltway consultants and 30-second TV ads, or whether we can transform it into a grassroots party of, by and for the working families of our country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What the choice between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen for Senate leader is all about | Bernie Sanders

articles.author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Aisha Down ; produced by Hana Williams ; senior producer Angus Neale ; executive producer Zoe Hitch
articles.description:
Jensen Huang’s resignation from the AI chipmaker Nvidia has sent shockwaves through the global economy. Huang resigned after reported affairs with an Nvidia executive and a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. The fallout is not over yet, with criticism mounting over the apparent lack of action from the US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick. Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s global technology reporter, Aisha Down
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why the Nvidia scandal is far from over - The Latest

articles.author: Editorial
articles.description:
From Cairo to Moscow to Washington, governments are turning up the pressure on media workers
Lina Attalah is an influential Egyptian journalist. Yet until last month, even she was unaware of a major and concerning piece of news: her own conviction. In 2024, a court issued her a one-year sentence for “spreading false news” and running a website without a licence – which she had repeatedly sought to obtain – after trying her in absentia, even though she was in the country. Ms Attalah learned of the case only after she was separately tried in October, resulting in a large fine and an order for the closure of the Mada Masr website. She faces retrial later this month.
Meanwhile, the entire newsroom of the fact-checking website Matsadash remain in detention weeks after authorities snatched the six journalists on charges including joining and financing a terrorist group and spreading false news. Their lawyers say that they have been tortured and forced to record fabricated confessions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Guardian view on press freedom: authoritarians target journalism because it matters | Editorial

articles.author: Brigid Schulte and Haley Swenson
articles.description:
Amid concerns over the influence of the manosphere, our findings show that young men are concerned about caregiving
When young men helped propel Donald Trump into the White House in 2024, the administration doubled down on a brand of toxic masculinity popular in the so-called manosphere.
They touted high testosterone, male supremacy, and a “biblically-based family” where men work and provide, and deferential women stay home to bear children and care for others.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Young men were key to the blue wave. Our research offers a reason why | Brigid Schulte and Haley Swenson

articles.author: Presented by Jonathan Freedland , with Susan Glasser, produced by Danielle Stephens and May Robson
articles.description:
Jonathan Freedland speaks to Susan Glasser of the New Yorker about why Trump’s judgment of high-profile men is questionable
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why the Nvidia cheating scandal is bad for Trump | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Presented by Lucy Hough with George Chidi ; produced by Angus Neale ; senior producer Leonore Schick ; executive producer Zoe Hitch
articles.description:
Mississippi has elected the Democrat Scott Colom in a historic race in the traditionally deep-red state, making him its first Black senator since shortly after the US civil war. The closely contested race was called more than a week after the US midterms, with Colom running against the Republican incumbent, Cindy Hyde-Smith. How did Colom’s grassroots campaign win despite limited early backing from national Democrats? Lucy Hough speaks to politics and democracy reporter George Chidi
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mississippi makes history with Democrat Scott Colom’s Senate win - The Latest

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright , produced by Anabel Bacon and Tiara Chiaramonte , engineered by Ivan Kuraev , executive producer Jonathan Menjivar
articles.description:
Pete Hegseth has managed to dodge an impeachment trial, for the second time. And Republicans have avoided — for now — a major public accounting of the damage done at the Pentagon during Hegseth’s tenure. Thomas Massie’s articles of impeachment detail charges that are likely to return when Democrats take the majority next year. Kai Wright speaks with Guardian senior political enterprise reporter Aram Roston about how people inside the military have reacted to the impeachment and to Hegseth’s tenure, from the boat strikes in the Caribbean to the massive loss of experienced leadership and a dramatic depletion of munitions in Iran. Roston, who has covered the Pentagon across several administrations, describes a Pentagon shaken up in ways he’s never before seen.

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pete Hegseth’s wake of destruction at the Pentagon – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Denis Campbell and Hanad Ahmed
articles.description:
NHS chiefs said last year that 43% of maternity and neonatal units in England do not meet safety standards
Ministers have been accused of “gambling with the safety of mothers and babies” after admitting they do not know how much repairing decrepit maternity units would cost.
NHS chiefs said last year that shoddy infrastructure meant 43% of maternity and neonatal units in England did not meet basic safety standards. Infrastructure problems hampered the delivery of clinical care thousands of times every year, NHS England said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ministers accused of ‘gambling with safety’ for not knowing cost of NHS maternity unit repairs

articles.author: Hannah Al-Othman
articles.description:
Survey respondents describe current or former partners controlling bank accounts and taking out credit online without full consent
Almost one in five young women and girls in the UK have experienced digital financial products being used as a tool of abuse by a current or former partner, a report has found.
Abusers are exploiting banking apps, online payments and digital credit to control young women, causing financial harm and preventing them from leaving relationships, according to research from the charity Surviving Economic Abuse.
In the UK, call the national domestic abuse helpline on 0808 2000 247, or visit Women’s Aid. In the US, the domestic violence hotline is 1-800-799-SAFE (7233). In Australia, the national family violence counselling service is on 1800 737 732. Other international helplines may be found via www.befrienders.org
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Digital finance products used to abuse almost 20% of young women and girls, UK report finds

articles.author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
articles.description:
Prime minister promises ‘root-and-branch rethink’ of support for young people as Milburn report advises sweeping changes to some benefits 

Andy Burnham: The crisis facing Britain’s young people is politicians’ fault. To fix it, we need a generational response

Andy Burnham has pledged to intervene as early as childhood to tackle youth unemployment before a watershed review, promising “a root-and-branch rethink of how we support childhood in the modern world”.
Burnham said the government would intervene at all the stages of life in which young people fell behind, and “long before they find themselves out of work and reliant on the state”, including providing more opportunities for vocational training in schools.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham pledges early intervention and ‘benefits backstop’ to tackle youth jobs crisis

articles.author: Lyndsey Winship
articles.description:
Exclusive: Trailer released for Rambert’s version of Russell T Davies’s show about friendship amid the 80s Aids crisis and the ‘extraordinary freedom’ of clubbing
Russell T Davies’s award-winning series It’s a Sin, about young gay friends living through the Aids crisis in 1980s London, is getting a new life as a dance piece, with a trailer released on Monday ahead of an opening at Aviva Studios in Manchester in February.
“We had a few approaches, but a lot of people wanted to make it a musical, which made my heart sink slightly,” said Davies. “I always imagined an aria between those two women on the seafront at the end and I thought: ‘Oh, that could be so terrible!’” Dance was different, he said. “It felt so original and so pure. The story distils down to these emotional moments that are going to be done so beautifully on stage.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Loaded with potential’: stage version of TV smash It’s a Sin has the dancefloor at its heart

articles.author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
articles.description:
Professor urges ministers to use awareness triggered by Russell Brand conviction to examine use of rape myths in trials
The debate triggered by high-profile cases must “pull back the curtain” on the treatment of people making allegations of sexual offences in the criminal justice system in England and Wales, the government’s independent adviser on rape has told the Guardian.
Prof Katrin Hohl, who has advised the government in an overhaul of how rape is treated by police forces and the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), said the government should use the public awareness triggered by Russell Brand’s conviction for rape to examine the use of rape myths and jury direction in trials.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Pull back the curtain’ on treatment of sexual assault victims in court, says UK government adviser

articles.author: Hannah Al-Othman
articles.description:
Calls for government to issue formal apology to those investigated after ending pregnancies in England and Wales
Campaigners and women previously convicted of illegal abortions have hailed a “historic day” after the pardoning of every woman who has faced criminal investigation for ending a pregnancy during the last 150 years.
A vote in the House of Lords earlier this year introduced legislation to pardon women accused of terminating their own pregnancies outside the legal framework and expunge their criminal records, under section 242 of the Crime and Policing Act 2026, which takes effect on Monday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Women prosecuted for abortions hail ‘historic day’ after receiving pardon

articles.author: Krishani Dhanji
articles.description:
Four countries call situation ‘entirely reversible’ in joint statement as flooding exacerbates humanitarian crisis
Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom and Italy have urged Israel to allow critical humanitarian aid to enter Gaza, describing the situation on the ground as “dire”.
The four nations released a joint statement on Monday urging Israel to allow 150,000 tents and other vital supplies being held at the border into Gaza ahead of winter, describing the situation on the ground as “dire”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia, UK, Canada and Italy urge Israel to allow critical aid to Gaza ahead of winter

articles.author: Harry Taylor
articles.description:
Duke of Sussex meets wounded veterans in city and says country could one day host Invictus Games
Prince Harry has told Ukrainian soldiers they are going to win the war with Russia, during a surprise visit to the country.
The Duke of Sussex met wounded veterans and medics in the city of Lviv, in the west of Ukraine, as he addressed a conference on treating those injured in war. He said he had taken a risk in travelling to the country, but that he had felt “warmth” when arriving on Saturday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Prince Harry tells Ukrainians they are ‘going to win war’ on surprise trip to Lviv

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
HMS Vengeance’s seven-month patrol prompts fears over slow pace of maintenance of ageing fleet and strain on crew
A Trident nuclear submarine has concluded a record seven-month deployment, returning to the Faslane naval base in Scotland where its crew was greeted by the defence secretary, Wes Streeting.
HMS Vengeance began its patrol on 12 April and spent 217 days submerged before returning on Sunday, having left the country when Keir Starmer was in Downing Street and Manchester United were third in the Premier League.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trident nuclear submarine concludes record underwater deployment

articles.author: Ben Quinn Political Correspondent
articles.description:
Total of 75 have already signed letter to Burnham opposing plans as discontent also grows over Europe and welfare changes
As many as 100 Labour MPs could sign a letter opposing the giant Rosebank oilfield, as discontent among backbenchers looks likely to surge this week, with rebellions also brewing over Europe and welfare changes.
A total of 75 MPs have already signed the private letter, which is expected to be delivered in the next fortnight to Andy Burnham as part of a campaign in which Labour MPs from the party’s 2024 intake are playing a significant role.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Labour rebellion over Rosebank oilfield expected to top 100 MPs

articles.author: Rob Davies
articles.description:
Chain restocks stores in operation named after singer of I Will Survive, as US owners release some of withheld funds
Poundland’s under-fire US owners have released funds to help the stricken discount chain restock shelves temporarily, keeping hopes of a rescue deal alive in the run-up to crunch talks with the government.
In an emergency resupply effort codenamed “Operation Gloria” by senior Poundland staff, about 16m grocery items were dispatched to 600 shops in the UK and Ireland over the weekend.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Poundland pins rescue hopes on Yorkshire Tea, Pot Noodle and Gloria Gaynor

articles.author: Harry Taylor
articles.description:
UKHSA warns of health impact on those vulnerable to cold and urges people to check in with neighbours 
Cold weather warnings have been issued for parts of the UK, and alerts for the risk to health services are due to begin on Sunday evening.
The Met Office issued yellow weather warnings for ice for central and eastern Scotland from 6pm on Sunday evening until 10am on Monday. People should be vigilant as they travelled, due to the risk from slipping on footpaths in icy conditions, it added.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cold and health alerts issued for Scotland and northern England as snow and ice expected

articles.author: Zoe Wood
articles.description:
From Aldi candles to Quince’s cashmere jumpers, cheaper dupes of high-end goods have gone mainstream. But is it fair?
For fans of the festive season nothing is more Christmassy than lighting a super-sized botanical candle with its trim of orange slices and berries.
But as the notes of cinnamon and clove fill the room will you be burning money spent on the White Company’s £95 “winter indulgence” candle that customers describe as the “scent of Christmas”. Or have you followed TikTok’s advice and bought the Aldi “dupe” for £25.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Who’s duping whom? Cut-price versions of luxury items are Christmas hit

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Exclusive: Shepard Fairey says image will hold PM accountable over promise to get people off the streets
The “Hope” portrait of Barack Obama by the US street artist Shepard Fairey came to symbolise a historic 2008 presidential campaign, became one of the most ubiquitous and reproduced political portraits of modern times, and ended up in the Smithsonian.
Fairey’s latest work, of the UK prime minister, Andy Burnham, may not elicit the same response but will, he hopes, deliver a hard-hitting message: one of a promise made.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Obama portrait artist draws Burnham for Big Issue cover to highlight rough sleeping vow

articles.author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
articles.description:
MP says party is being squeezed by arrival of ‘more plausible’ Labour leader in Andy Burnham
Reform UK has been losing support to Labour after “a very difficult year”, Danny Kruger has said, just over 12 months after his defection to Nigel Farage’s party.
The MP, who has been tasked with preparing Reform for government, denied he regretted jumping from the Conservatives as recent polls indicated a Tory revival under Kemi Badenoch.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Reform UK losing support to Labour after ‘difficult year’, says Danny Kruger

articles.author: Jasper Jolly
articles.description:
Liberty Steel Dalzell plant in Motherwell with order for 34,000 tonnes of metal plate to build three warships has struggled to pay bills
The Royal Navy is facing questions over whether three new warships will be built with British steel as its Scottish supplier faces deepening financial difficulties.
Liberty Steel Dalzell, a plate mill in Motherwell, has struggled to pay its bills and workers in recent weeks, according to several people with knowledge of operations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Troubled Scottish steel supplier raises questions over Royal Navy contracts

articles.author: Raphael Boyd and Mark Brown
articles.description:
Mia Latter says she was in an abusive relationship with the convicted rapist when he was 30 and she was 16
A woman who alleges she was raped by Russell Brand when she was 16 has waived her right to anonymity to campaign for a staggered age of consent.
Mia Latter says she was in an abusive three-month relationship with Brand when he was 30 and she was 16.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russell Brand accuser waives anonymity to call for consent law change

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
articles.description:
Delayed deliveries and inspection hold-ups among issues facing hauliers navigating post-Brexit border processes
Three small boxes of spinach and ricotta cannelloni destined for a supermarket in Gibraltar languish on an EU inspector’s bench at the Eurotunnel terminal in Calais.
They have been removed from a truck laden with perishables for British food lovers on the Rock – Morrisons steak and ale pie, family-size blocks of Morrisons cheddar cheese, ‘M’ Best coleslaw from Avondale foods in Craigavon in Northern Ireland and long-life milk.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pasta, pies and paperwork errors: the reality of Brexit food checks

articles.author: Jane Clinton and Nicola Slawson
articles.description:
In the second in our series, four young Britons reveal how the search has taken a toll on their mental and physical health

‘The social contract is broken’: young people on feeling shut out of careers

Guardian to follow lives of eight young people in their search for jobs

“I had to quit and move back in with my parents because I had developed ME/chronic fatigue syndrome. I am now housebound and cannot look after myself. Although I cannot prove it, I strongly believe that prolonged period of high stress played a big part in the decline of my health.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I’m scared about my future’: young people on the stress and desperation of jobseeking

articles.author: Mark Sweney
articles.description:
Exclusive: British sportswear firm is seeking to obtain rights to The Conditioning Club, which is also the name of a Gloucestershire gym
Gymshark, the £1bn British sportswear firm started in a family garage, is locked in a trademark battle that threatens the future of a small fitness business.
Ben Francis, the university dropout who started sewing his own gym clothes in his parents’ garage and is now estimated to be worth £800m, is trying to add The Conditioning Club to his Gymshark stable of trademarks.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Gymshark in trademark battle that threatens future of small fitness business

articles.author: Anna Bawden
articles.description:
Exclusive: 2,850 more patients a month would need to be treated within 62 days to meet March 2027 goal, as experts warn of failure of leadership
Nearly 10,000 more cancer patients in England will not be treated on time because the government will fail to meet its targets, amid a failure of leadership, focus and resource, experts have warned.
The NHS set an interim target to treat 80% of cancer patients within 62 days of urgent referral or consultant upgrade by March 2027. But with little more than 100 days to go, the proportion of patients starting treatment on time in September was 70.7%, down from 71.9% in August, NHS figures show.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NHS England on track to miss key cancer treatment target by 10,000 patients

articles.author: Donna Ferguson
articles.description:
Comedian regrets ‘inappropriate’ jokes he made with Brand during work pair did together in the 2000s
The Great British Bake Off presenter Noel Fielding has said he was “horrified and deeply disturbed to learn of Russell Brand’s crimes” and has had no contact with his fellow comedian “for many years”.
In the early 2000s, Fielding often worked with Brand, who was sentenced to more than 10 years in prison on Monday for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Noel Fielding ‘horrified and deeply disturbed’ by Russell Brand’s crimes

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Charles marks 78th birthday and 50th anniversary of King’s Trust charity with a playlist for special episode of podcast
King Charles marked his 78th birthday on Saturday joking with Elton John that they were “still standing” as he appeared on the singer-songwriter’s Rocket Hour for a shared musical journey.
In a special recorded episode of the Apple Radio show to mark the 50th anniversary of the monarch’s charity the King’s Trust, Charles’s playlist included John’s I’m Still Standing.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Still standing’: king jokes as he appears on Elton John’s Rocket Hour

articles.author: Steven Morris
articles.description:
Paintings by one of country’s most important artists have been animated and set to music at National Library of Wales
The paintings of artists such as Vincent van Gogh, Paul Cézanne and David Hockney have been brought to life in all-singing, all-dancing immersive shows in recent years.
Now one of Wales’s most important artists, Sir Kyffin Williams, known for capturing the spectacular landscapes of his homeland with layers of paint thickly applied with a palette knife, has been given the same treatment.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Immersive show brings Kyffin Williams’ rugged Welsh landscapes to life

articles.author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: investigation finds prescriptions for children under 12, as experts stress need for specialist supervision and long-term monitoring
Hundreds of children in England are receiving prescriptions for GLP-1 medications, including some younger than 12, the Guardian can reveal.
GLP-1 medications were initially developed to help people with type 2 diabetes control their blood sugar levels, but have since become a popular slimming aid, with products such as Wegovy and Mounjaro becoming household names.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hundreds of children in England prescribed weight-loss jabs, figures show

articles.author: Joe Pinner
articles.description:
Five-year project will create wildlife corridors by building wetlands and increase access to green and blue spaces
Bristol could become home to the UK’s first “wetland city” thanks to a charity’s efforts to create vast wildlife corridors that will reduce flood risk and give people more access to green and blue spaces.
The Wildfowl & Wetlands Trust (WWT) said the five-year initiative would include more than 200 projects to restore and create wetlands across the city. These will range from small household rainwater ponds and street-level rain gardens to restoring river habitats, reconnecting rivers with their floodplains, and creating new wetlands.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bristol aims to become UK’s first ‘wetland city’ and reduce flood risk

articles.author: Vikram Dodd and Hannah Al-Othman
articles.description:
Hospitals, GPs, police forces and property agents have had to find a workaround for Microsoft packages
Hospitals, GPs, police forces and property agents across the UK have been hit by the global Microsoft outage. Here’s how the disruption to email and other IT facilities has affected key services.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How Microsoft outage has affected key public services in the UK

articles.author: Ben Quinn, Aisha Down, Andrew Gregory and Jamie Grierson
articles.description:
NHS suffering ‘serious’ and widespread disruption, while people are told of possible delays in receiving prescriptions
Vital UK services have been hit by a global Microsoft outage that left hospital staff resorting to paper records and fuelled concerns about an over-reliance on a small number of tech companies.
A day of widespread disruption sent some sectors back to the 1990s, with court staff looking for fax machines and rail travellers being warned they might not be able to rely on digital tickets.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Microsoft outage hits hospitals, GPs, schools and police across UK

articles.author: Daniel Boffey Chief reporter
articles.description:
It has been suggested that women with stories to tell felt silenced after signing non-disclosure agreements
The UK’s minister for women has suggested that the government has not gone far enough in tackling the abusive use of non-disclosure agreements.
Bridget Phillipson was commenting in the context of the allegations of improper behaviour by David Walliams – which he denies – and the conviction of Russell Brand for rape and sexual assault. In both cases, it has been suggested that women with stories to tell felt silenced after signing an NDA.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: After Walliams and Brand, how could the UK government tackle NDAs?

articles.author: Josh Taylor, Aisha Down and Mark Sweney
articles.description:
Problem affects businesses, government agencies and even tech firm’s own employees

Microsoft scrambles to fix global outage affecting Teams and Outlook

Microsoft outage – live updates

Tell us: have you been affected by the Microsoft outage?

Millions of people were unable to access their emails, Teams chats or meetings on Thursday night and Friday after a Microsoft 365 outage brought down services across the globe.
The outage has lasted for more than 21 hours, with meaningful signs of recovery visible beginning shortly before midday GMT on Friday. It affected businesses, government agencies and even Microsoft employees all over the world. Those reporting issues have included the US House of Representatives, an Australian spy agency, airlines in India, European government agencies, and police services, ambulances and hospitals in the UK.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: A global Microsoft 365 outage has hit millions – what happened and when will it be fixed?

articles.author: Matthew Pearce and Pippa Neill
articles.description:
Exclusive: Government in ‘private meetings’ about removing cost cap protections under Aarhus convention
The government is considering stripping back legal protections that limit the costs community groups face when challenging planning decisions that threaten nature.
The Aarhus convention, an environmental treaty that was signed into law by the UK in 2005, guarantees the legal right to participate in democratic processes on environmental matters – such as sewage pollution, new roads or datacentre developments.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Right to make green challenges to planning decisions under threat, say UK lawyers

articles.author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
articles.description:
Siberian rubythroat was thousands of miles off course from its route to winter in south or south-east Asia
A bird that flies south from its breeding grounds in Siberia to winter in south and south-east Asia has been found thousands of miles off course in Cumbria. Regrettably, it was found by a cat.
Chris Hind, Cumbria’s county recorder for birds, said it was “extraordinary” that a Siberian rubythroat was found on his patch, albeit dead. There have been only 17 recorded instances of the bird in the UK, 15 of those in the northern Scottish isles.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Incredibly unusual’ bird migrating from Siberia found in Cumbria – killed by cat

articles.author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
articles.description:
Increase reported by Aviva after Hastings Direct said claims were up 140% in August and Axa said it had been a ‘surge year’
The UK’s largest insurer has been hit by a rise in subsidence claims after an extremely hot summer left households across the country grappling with the fallout from the growing climate crisis.
Aviva said on Friday it had experienced the jump amid an industry-wide surge in households filing subsidence claims with their insurers to cover repairs, which typically are needed to address cracks, sloping floors, and off-kilter doors and windows.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK’s biggest insurer hit by rise in subsidence claims after record hot summer
